newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-LIBERTADORES SEMI-FINALS LEFT FINELY BALANCED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIBERTADORES SEMI-FINALS LEFT FINELY BALANCED.

text.p: The South American Liberadores Cup semi-finals were both finely balanced after the two home teams managed single-goal victories in Wednesday's first leg games.

Racing Club, winners of the competition in 1967, beat Peru's Sporting Cristal 3-2 in Buenos Aires while Brazilians Cruzeiro beat Colo Colo of Chile 1-0 in Belo Horizonte after a blunder by goalkeeper Marcelo Ramirez.
As a result, next week's second leg matches could result in Sporting and Colo Colo, who are considered the underdogs, both reaching the final.

The semi-finalists had to wait almost two months for the ties as the tournament was interrupted to make way for the Copa America, held in Bolivia in June, and two rounds of World Cup qualifying matches.
In Buenos Aires, Argentina's Racing Club were leading 3-1 and in a relatively comfortable position until Luis Bonet pulled a crucial goal back for Sporting five minutes from the end.

Playing before a 60,000 crowd, the teams went in level at halftime after Sporting's Peruvian international Jorge Soto scored in the 42nd minute to wipe out a 30th minute goal by Diego Martin Vilallonga.

Two goals in six minutes by Claudio Ubeda put Racing Club, who have had more success in international competition than in the Argentine championship, in a commanding position early in the second half.
But Bonet's late strike gave Sporting a fighting chance of becoming the first team from their country to reach a Libertadores final.

Racing are one of the biggest clubs in their country but have suffered a dearth of titles since their last Argentine championship win in 1966 although they won the Libertadores the following year and the South American Supercup in 1988.
Cruzeiro, still recovering from a 5-0 mauling at home to Sao Paulo in a Brazilian championship game last week, got a perfect start when striker Marcelo put them ahead after just seven minutes.
Marcelo's goal came after Colo Colo goalkeeper Marcelo Ramirez tried to dribble the ball out of his area but lost the ball to Cruzeiro striker Cleisson.
But the 1976 champions failed to add to their total and now face the difficult task of defending their lead in Santiago against the only Chilean team to have lifted the trophy.
